POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel Cancel an order by its pick ticket ID. This works only before the order has shipping or tracking information and while it is still open; otherwise the response says the order could not be cancelled. Cancel by your pick ticket. The response is 200 whenever the request is valid; read order_cancelled to see whether it worked. Orders are created in the background, usually within seconds of a successful submit. Until then, cancel answers that the order cannot be cancelled: wait a few seconds and try again. Only open orders with no shipping or tracking information can be cancelled. Assembly orders cannot be cancelled through the API, and cancel finds only orders placed under your own owner code (not a related account's). If the order had already been released to the warehouse, a successful cancel marks it "do not ship" in Capacity, but contact Capacity Support straight away so the warehouse can stop it. Keep pick tickets unique. If two open orders share one, which order is cancelled is not defined. Existing integrations. POST /api/v1/auth/token Exchange your client ID and secret for a bearer token. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token> on every other call. Tokens last about 15 minutes; expires_in in the response gives the exact number of seconds. Form post, not JSON. Send grant_type=client_credentials with your client_id and client_secret, either as form fields or as an HTTP Basic Authorization header (client_id:client_secret, base64). If both are present, the header is used. Secrets are case-sensitive. Reuse the token. It lasts about 15 minutes (expires_in, in seconds). Cache it and request a new one shortly before it expires; do not request a token per call. Errors use the OAuth shape, not {"message": ...}: 400 {"error": "invalid_credentials", "error_description": ...}, 400 {"error": "unsupported_grant_type"}, and 503 {"error": "temporarily_unavailable", "error_description": ...} when the token service is briefly unavailable (retry with backoff). The Partner API uses the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow. Your integration exchanges a client ID and secret for a short-lived access token, then sends that token on every request.

Credential Format Notes Client ID Text, issued by Capacity Not secret, but do not publish it. Client secret Text, issued by Capacity Secret and case-sensitive. Sandbox and production credentials are issued separately. See Environments.

POST /api/v1/auth/token with a form body (application/x-www-form-urlencoded): Field Value grant_type client_credentials (the only grant supported) client_id Your client ID client_secret Your client secret You can send the ID and secret as an HTTP Basic Authorization header instead of form fields. If you send both, the header is used. cURL # Form fields curl -X POST "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token" \ -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \ --data-urlencode "grant_type=client_credentials" \ --data-urlencode "client_id=$CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID" \ --data-urlencode "client_secret=$CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET" # Or HTTP Basic curl -X POST "https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token" \ -u "$CAPACITY_CLIENT_ID:$CAPACITY_CLIENT_SECRET" \ -d "grant_type=client_credentials" The response: Field Meaning access_token The token. Treat it as an opaque string: do not parse it or rely on its contents. token_type Always bearer. expires_in Seconds until the token expires (about 900). .issued, .expires When the token was issued and expires, as RFC 1123 dates in GMT.
Send it on every request except the token request: Request header Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9.EXAMPLE-ONLY.signature

Request a token once and reuse it until about 60 seconds before it expires. Requesting a token for every call is slower for you and may be limited in future. token; private DateTimeOffset expiresAt; public async Task<string> GetTokenAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { await gate.WaitAsync(cancellationToken); try { if (token is not null && DateTimeOffset.UtcNow < expiresAt.AddSeconds(-60)) { return token; } using var response = await http.PostAsync("https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token", new FormUrlEncodedContent(new Dictionary<string, string> { ["grant_type"] = "client_credentials", ["client_id"] = clientId, ["client_secret"] = clientSecret, }), cancellationToken); response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode(); using var json = JsonDocument.Parse(await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(cancellationToken)); token = json.RootElement.GetProperty("access_token").GetString()!; expiresAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddSeconds(json.RootElement.GetProperty("expires_in").GetInt32()); return token; } finally { gate.Release(); } } } On a 401 If a call returns 401, the token may have expired early or been revoked. Get a new token and retry the call once. If it fails again, stop and check your credentials.

Response Cause Fix 400 {"error": "invalid_credentials", ...} Wrong or missing client ID or secret, or the credentials are disabled. Check both values and the case of the secret. Check you are not using sandbox credentials in production. 400 {"error": "unsupported_grant_type"} grant_type is missing or not client_credentials. Send grant_type=client_credentials. 503 {"error": "temporarily_unavailable", ...} The token service is briefly unavailable. Retry after a few seconds, with backoff. 401 on any other call Missing, malformed or expired token. Get a new token and retry once.

The 940 tells Capacity to ship an order from your stock. Each transaction set (ST to SE) is one order. A file can carry many orders in one functional group. Direction You to Capacity Version and GS01 004010, OW Folder IN in your folder When Every 10 minutes from 00:50 to 22:50; files that arrive later are picked up at 00:50, US Eastern Answered by A 997 in the same run, then a 945 when the order ships The Envelopes page describes the ISA, GS, GE and IEA segments that wrap the file.

W0502 is your order number. It comes back in the 945 W0602. W0505 is your pick ticket number. Use a new pick ticket for every order. Capacity holds an order that repeats an earlier one for review as a possible duplicate. The 945 echoes your W0503 purchase order number (W0606), W0505 pick ticket (W0607) and W0504 link sequence number (W0608). Send these if you match shipments with them. Send a ship-to N1 loop (N101 ST) with N3 and N4 on every order. Send N9 CU with the retailer (customer) code agreed during onboarding. It tells Capacity which retailer's rules apply to the order. Send one LX loop for each order line. W0105 identifies the item: use the UPC or SKU that Capacity holds for it. For a prepack, send the prepack item with W0116 PPK. Capacity ships its components. Do not send component (SLN) lines on their own. Capacity chooses lots when it picks, so a lot number in W0113 is not used. Segments that X12 allows but are not listed here are accepted and not used.

The 943 tells Capacity that stock is on its way to the warehouse. Each transaction set becomes one receiving order. When the stock arrives, Capacity receives it against that receiving order. Direction You to Capacity Version and GS01 004010, AR Folder IN in your folder When Every 10 minutes from 00:50 to 22:50; files that arrive later are picked up at 00:50, US Eastern Answered by A 997 in the same run, then a 944 when the receiving order is closed The Envelopes page describes the ISA, GS, GE and IEA segments that wrap the file.

documents.t: W0602 is your receiving order (purchase order) number. Use a new value for each receiving order. It comes back in the 944 W1704. W0604 is your shipment ID, for example the container number. It comes back in the 944 W1705. Send G62 17 with the date the stock is expected at the warehouse. Send W27 on every 943. Capacity records the SCAC and routing when W2701 is T. Send one W04 loop for each item. Identify the item in W0404 and W0405 with its style (VN), UPC (UP) or SKU (SK). Send N9 LI with your line number on each item if you want it back in the 944. Send the lot number in W0414 LT and W0415 for lot-controlled stock. Send your 832 for new items before the 943, so every item is known when the stock arrives. Segments that X12 allows but are not listed here, such as N3, N4, PER and G61, are accepted and not used.

documents.t: Match the 944 to your 943 with W1704 (your 943 W0602). W1705 returns your 943 W0604 shipment ID when you sent one. W1703 is Capacity's receipt number for the receiving order. Each W07 loop reports one item: the quantity received in eaches, the 12-digit UPC in W0705 and your SKU or style in W0707. A prepack is reported as one W07 loop for each component, with the component quantities. N9 LI returns the line number from your 943 N9 LI. W1401 is the total quantity received, the sum of every W0701. Compare W0701 with the quantities in your 943 to find shortages and overages. Some options, such as the second item ID in W0706 and W0707 and lot reporting, are agreed during onboarding.

A 997 says whether a functional group passed the X12 syntax check, and which transaction sets in it were accepted or rejected. It does not confirm business content: a shipment is confirmed by the 945, a receipt by the 944. Version and GS01 004010, FA Capacity sends One 997 for every 940, 943 and 832 file, to OUT, in the same run that processes your file, normally within minutes You may send One 997 for each 945 and 944 file, to IN or the folder agreed during onboarding. Optional The Envelopes page describes the ISA, GS, GE and IEA segments that wrap the file.

Capacity acknowledges every group it receives. AK1 returns your GS01 and GS06. Each AK2 loop returns the ST01 and ST02 of one transaction set, and AK5 gives its result. AK9 (group) Meaning What Capacity does A Accepted Processes every transaction set. E Accepted, errors noted Processes the accepted sets. AK3 and AK4 describe the errors. P Partially accepted Processes the sets with AK5 A or E. Sets with AK5 R are not processed. R Rejected Processes nothing from the group. Every X12 file you exchange with Capacity is one interchange: an ISA header, one functional group (GS to GE) and an IEA trailer. Inside the group, each transaction set starts with ST and ends with SE. Envelope structure ISA Interchange control header GS Functional group header ST Transaction set header ... segments of the set ... SE Transaction set trailer (more ST to SE sets of the same type) GE Functional group trailer IEA Interchange control trailer

Delimiter Character Notes Element separator * The character after ISA sets it Component (sub-element) separator > ISA16 Segment terminator ~ The character after ISA16 Capacity reads the delimiters from the ISA of each file you send, so the characters above are recommended rather than required. A carriage return and line feed (CR LF) after each ~ is accepted. Files Capacity sends always use *, > and ~, with CR LF after each ~, so each segment is on its own line. Capacity replaces any of these characters that appear inside a data value with a space.

During onboarding you and Capacity agree each side's interchange ID qualifier (ISA05 and ISA07) and ID (ISA06 and ISA08). The examples in these guides use: Party Qualifier ID You (example) ZZ Mutually defined PARTNEREXAMPLE Capacity 08 UCC EDI communications ID CAPACITY GS02 and GS03 carry the same IDs, without the padding to 15 characters. In files Capacity sends, the IDs are reversed: Capacity is the sender.

The ISA has a fixed width. Every element is padded to its full length, so the segment is always 106 characters including the terminator. Put every X12 file you send in your IN folder. Give every file a unique name, for example 940-20261110-153000.edi. Upload under a temporary name, then rename the file when the upload has finished. A half-written file is then never picked up. Send one interchange per file (one ISA to IEA), with one functional group of one set type. A group can hold many transaction sets, for example many orders in one 940 file. Capacity picks up X12 files every 10 minutes from 00:50 to 22:50 US Eastern. The Connecting page lists the times for each set.
Capacity writes the 945, 944 and 997 files it sends to your OUT folder. Every file name is unique. Download each file, then delete it or move it out of the folder. Capacity keeps its own copy.

Capacity sends a 997 for every 940, 943 and 832 file it receives. The 997 is written in the same run that processes your file, normally within minutes. Capacity checks each file against the X12 4010 syntax rules and the usage in these guides. The 997 tells you the result: 997 result What Capacity does A Accepted Processes every transaction set in the group. E Accepted, errors noted Processes the accepted sets. The 997 lists the errors so that you can correct future files. P Partially accepted Processes the accepted sets. The rejected sets are listed in AK5 with code R. Correct and resend only those sets. R Rejected Processes nothing from the file. Correct the file and send it again with new control numbers. You can send a 997 back for each 945 and 944. It is optional, and Capacity records the result. See 997 functional acknowledgment. :::tip Check every 997 A rejected set never becomes an order, a receiving order or a product. Watch for 997s with AK5 or AK9 code R or P, and resend the rejected sets. :::

A transaction set that passes the syntax check is processed even when its content needs attention. For example, a 940 for an unknown SKU or an unknown ship method still creates the order. Capacity holds that order for review and works with you to release it. Send your product catalog before your first orders so that every SKU is known.

Email itedi@capacityllc.com with the sets you plan to exchange. Agree your interchange ID qualifier and ID, and Capacity's, as described on the Envelopes page. Agree the options that some sets offer. For example, a 945 can carry carton detail (MAN and PAL for every carton) or report order lines only. Send test files with ISA15 set to T. Capacity sends test files with ISA15 T while you test. When the tests pass, switch to ISA15 P. From then on, Capacity sends production files with ISA15 P. Capacity identifies your files by the folder they arrive in, so use only your own folder.

The base URLs on Environments have no trailing slash, and every path starts with one, so join them as they are: https://api-partner.capacityllc.com + /api/v1/auth/token = https://api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/v1/auth/token If your configured base URL ends in /, the request goes to https://api-partner.capacityllc.com//api/v1/auth/token. The API does not merge repeated slashes, at either address, so that request matches no route and returns 404 with an empty body: Path called Response /api/v1/ping 200 with a valid token, 401 without one //api/v1/ping 404, empty body /Token (previous REST API) 200 with valid credentials, 400 with invalid ones //Token (previous REST API) 404, empty body To fix it, remove the trailing slash from the base URL in your configuration, or trim it in code before adding the path. These rules apply to every flat file. Each file's own page adds its columns and any rules of its own.

Tab-delimited text. One record per line. Lines end with CR LF; Capacity also accepts LF in files you send. Header row first. Every file starts with one header row that names the columns. The header row is required in files you send. Columns by position. Capacity reads columns by their position, not by the header names. Send every column of the layout in the documented order, even when it is empty. Empty values. Leave an optional column empty by putting nothing between its two tabs. Do not write NULL. No tabs or line breaks inside values. Remove them before you write the file.
Send UTF-8 text, with or without a byte order mark. Plain ASCII is UTF-8 too. Files Capacity sends are UTF-8 without a byte order mark.

Dates you send are MM/DD/YYYY unless the column says otherwise. Dates are US Eastern calendar dates. Capacity operates in US Eastern time. Decimals use a dot (12.50) and no thousands separator. Do not add currency symbols or percent signs. Whole-number columns accept digits only.

Owner code (ClientCode). Your two-character code, issued by Capacity at onboarding. It must be the same on every line. SKU. Every SKU in an order or receiving order must already exist in Capacity. Send new products in a product upload file or X12 832 first. Yes/no columns use Y or N; flag columns in the product file use 1 or 0.

The inventory file gives you the stock balance of your products at the end of the day. It is a full snapshot, not a list of changes. For changes during the day, use the inventory adjustments file. Direction Capacity to you Folder OUT/Inventory in your folder on ftp01.capacityllc.com When Daily at 23:50 US Eastern What it holds One line per product with its balance at the time the file was written. Version 5.0 has one line per lot.

OnHand is everything in the warehouse for the SKU, including stock that is committed, on hold or in quarantine. Commited is stock already allocated to orders that have not shipped yet. The column header is spelled Commited. OnHand excludes stock on hold or in quarantine; those are reported in their own columns where the layout has them. Available is the stock you can sell: OnHand less Commited. Use it to update the stock levels in your store. Quantities are in units (eaches). The file name carries the date, for example Daily_Inventory_ZZ_20261110.txt. There is one file per day; if Capacity writes the file again the same day, the new file replaces the earlier one. Replace your stock levels with the values in the file. Do not add them to the previous day's values. Pick up each file, then delete it or move it out of the folder. Capacity keeps a copy.

Version 3.0 has the eight core columns. Version 4.0 adds on-hold and quarantine quantities and three reference columns. Version 5.0 adds the lot number and expiry date, with one line per lot. New clients choose version 4.0 (one line per SKU) or version 5.0 (one line per lot). Version 3.0 is kept for existing clients.

The inventory adjustments file lists changes to your stock made in the warehouse, such as count corrections and damaged stock. Use it to keep your stock levels in step between inventory files. Direction Capacity to you Folder OUT/InventoryDelta in your folder on ftp01.capacityllc.com When Every 30 minutes from 06:35 to 20:35 US Eastern. No file is written when nothing changed. What it holds One line per stock movement recorded since the previous file. Each movement appears in one file only.

Quantity is the change, not the new balance. A positive number adds units to your stock; a negative number removes them. Apply the files in the order of the time in their names, InventoryDelta-yyyy-MM-dd-HH-mm-ss.txt (24-hour clock, US Eastern). TransactionType is ADJ for an inventory adjustment. Other transaction codes may appear for other kinds of stock movement. Apply them the same way, using Quantity. Receipts are not in this file. They are reported in the receiving confirmation. Pick up each file, then delete it or move it out of the folder. Capacity keeps a copy.

The order file sends Capacity the orders you want shipped. Each line is one order line, with the order details repeated on every line of the order. Direction You to Capacity Folder IN in your folder on ftp01.capacityllc.com When Every 5 minutes from 00:48 to 23:18, Sunday to Friday; every 10 minutes on Saturday, US Eastern After processing Capacity moves the file to an archive and adds a batch number to the front of its name The flat file rules apply to every layout on this page.

Header row, then one line per order line. Capacity reads columns by position, so every line has every column of your layout, in order, even when a value is empty. EndOfLine is always EOL. It is the last column of versions 3.0, 4.0 and 4.1. One PickTicketID per order. All lines of an order share the same PickTicketID, and the order-level columns (ship-to, ship method, dates and amounts) must be identical on every line of the order. Unique order numbers. Use a new PickTicketID for every order. If Capacity receives a PickTicketID it already has, it holds the new order as a duplicate for review. Your owner code. ClientCode must be your two-character owner code on every line. A file with another owner code is rejected. A ship-to name. Send ShipBusinessName, ShipName or both. Release lines take the name from the EDI purchase order. Known SKUs. Every ItemProductID must already exist in Capacity, as a Capacity SKU or an alternate SKU. Send new products first. Whole-number quantities. Quantities are whole numbers of units, digits only, with no thousands separator. Dates. Use MM/DD/YYYY, US Eastern. YYYY-MM-DD is also accepted.

ShipMethod must match one of the ship methods set up for your account, character for character. Capacity gives you the list during onboarding and adds methods on request. Email itedi@capacityllc.com to ask for a new one. An order with an empty or unknown ShipMethod is still imported. Capacity holds it until the ship method is corrected, then releases it to the warehouse. Send a ship method from your list to avoid the delay. The ship confirmation reports the carrier service actually used, under Capacity's own service name. See the ship confirmation file.

ItemOrderQuantity is the quantity your customer ordered. ItemShipQuantity is the quantity to ship. Leave it empty to ship the ordered quantity. When you send ItemShipQuantity, Capacity ships that quantity, even when it is lower than the ordered quantity. A value of 0 creates a line with nothing to ship.

Some retailers send their purchase orders to Capacity by EDI (an X12 850) on your behalf. Capacity holds each of these orders until you release it, so that you decide what ships and when. To release one, add a line to an order file for each product to ship: Set ReleaseFlag to Y. Set CapacityImportID to Capacity's import number for the EDI order. Capacity gives you this number. Repeat the PONumber, RetailerCode and StoreNumber of the EDI order. Give the order your own PickTicketID, and set ClientCode, ItemProductID, ItemOrderQuantity and ItemShipQuantity. Leave the ship-to columns and ShipMethod empty. Capacity uses the address and routing of the EDI order. The third line of each sample file below is a release line.
Each order in a file is imported on its own. If Capacity asks you to resend an order, send only that order in a new file, not the whole file again.

The product upload file creates your products (SKUs) in Capacity and updates some of their details. Send it before the first order or receiving order that uses a new SKU. Each line describes one SKU. Direction You to Capacity Folder IN/NewSkus in your folder on ftp01.capacityllc.com When Every 30 minutes from 06:45 to 20:45 US Eastern, Monday to Saturday What it does Creates each SKU that does not exist yet, and updates the details a file can change for each SKU that does The flat file rules apply: tab-delimited, a header row first, columns read by position. Send all 30 columns on every line, and no more.

Each SKU must be unique within your account. A SKU may appear only once in a file. Do not use spaces in a SKU. Capacity stores SKUs in upper case, so sku-example-1 and SKU-EXAMPLE-1 are the same SKU. A SKU is locked once it is created. A line with a different SKU creates a new product; it never renames an existing one. If the product has no UPC, repeat the SKU in the UPC column.

Weights are in pounds and dimensions in inches, for a full case. CaseCube is the case volume in cubic feet: length × width × height in inches, divided by 1728. A 12 × 10 × 8 inch case is 0.5556 cubic feet. Flag columns (TrackSerialNo, IsHazmat, TrackLotNumber, TrackExpiryDate) take 1 for yes and 0 for no. CountryOfOrigin is the full country name, for example United States. Prices and other decimals use a dot and no currency symbol or thousands separator.

When a line names a SKU that already exists, the file updates these columns only: UPC, Brand, Category, RetailPrice, TrackSerialNo, CountryOfOrigin, HarmonizationCode, StyleNumber, ColorCode, SizeCode, NMFC, CommodityDesc, Class and the three availability columns. The other columns are set when the SKU is created, and a later file does not change them: Name UOM, CaseQuantity and NoOfInnerPacks CaseWeight, CaseLength, CaseWidth, CaseHeight and CaseCube IsHazmat, TrackLotNumber, TrackExpiryDate and ShelfLifeInDays To change any of these for an existing SKU, contact Capacity at itedi@capacityllc.com.

Capacity rejects the whole file when a whole-number column holds a decimal or text, a price holds a currency symbol, a UPC contains a dot, or a SKU appears twice. A line with an unknown UOM, or a SKU or Category longer than its maximum length, is rejected on its own. A rejected file is moved to the BAD folder and reviewed by Capacity. Fix the file and send it again under a new name.

Receiving uses two files. You send a receiving order file to tell Capacity what stock is on its way. Capacity writes a receiving confirmation file to tell you what was received. All quantities in the receiving confirmation file are in units. The flat file rules apply to both files.

Direction You to Capacity Folder IN/ReceivingOrder in your folder on ftp01.capacityllc.com When Every 15 minutes from 04:44 to 22:44 US Eastern, every day What it does Creates one receiving order for each PONumber in the file

Every SKU must already exist in Capacity. Send new products in a product upload file first. If a line names a SKU that does not exist yet, Capacity holds the whole receiving order. It tries again every 15 minutes for 7 days, so the receiving order is created as soon as the product exists. The units expected on a line are Quantity × CasePack. To send units, set CasePack to 1. UnitofMeasure is for your reference only. If the same SKU appears on more than one line of a receiving order, Capacity adds the lines together into one line. In version 2.0, a LotNumber must already be set up in Capacity for that SKU. Contact Capacity to set up lots before you send them.

To change a receiving order, send the whole receiving order again with the same PONumber and ContainerNumber. If Capacity has not started receiving it, the new file replaces the earlier receiving order. Once receiving has started, a file with the same PONumber creates a separate receiving order. Contact Capacity to change a receiving order that is already being received.

The Partner API has two environments. They have different base URLs, different credentials and different data. Nothing you do in one affects the other. Sandbox Production Base URL https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com https://api-partner.capacityllc.com Credentials Sandbox client ID and secret Production client ID and secret Data Test data. Orders are not fulfilled or shipped to real customers. Live. Orders are picked, packed and shipped. Use it for Building and testing your integration Your live integration, after go-live Use the Sandbox | Production switch at the top of every page to change the base URL in all code samples. The coloured band under the navigation bar shows which one is selected. New integrations use api-partner New integrations must use api-partner.capacityllc.com. Capacity does not support new integrations at any other address.

Integrations built against the previous Capacity REST API call https://api-integration.capacityllc.com. That address is moving to this same API, so existing integrations keep working without changes: The previous paths (for example POST /api/order/create and POST /Token) keep working for existing integrations at both api-integration.capacityllc.com and api-partner.capacityllc.com. The request and response formats do not change. api-integration.capacityllc.com is for existing integrations only. It is not offered to new clients: a new integration calling an /api/v1/ path there gets 410 Gone with the api-partner address to use. Capacity will ask existing integrations to move to api-partner.capacityllc.com and the /api/v1/ paths. See Paths and versions and the legacy path map in the API reference.

Keep the base URL in configuration. Your code should read one setting for the base URL and one for each credential. Going live, or moving from api-integration to api-partner, is then a configuration change, not a code change. Never mix the pairs. A sandbox token is rejected by production and a production token is rejected by the sandbox. A configuration that points production credentials at the sandbox URL fails in a way that is easy to misread as "wrong password". Label your logs. Log which environment each request went to, and the X-Correlation-ID you sent.

Each environment has an interactive Swagger page at <base URL>/api/swagger. For example, the sandbox page is https://uat-api-partner.capacityllc.com/api/swagger. It needs a personal login. Ask for a login. Email itedi@capacityllc.com from your company's contact on record, with the name and work email of each person who needs one. Every person gets their own login. Do not share a login. Set it up. You get an email from Capacity Partner API (no-reply@capacityllc.com). Its link works for 72 hours. Choose a password: at least 12 characters, with upper and lower case, a digit and a symbol. Then add the login to a phone authenticator app (Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator or FreeOTP). Every sign-in asks for the 6-digit code from the app. Sign in at the Swagger page with your email, your password and the code. Authorize. Click Authorize and enter your company's client ID and secret. Your login only opens the page; the client ID and secret decide which data you see. A Swagger login can use only your own company's client IDs, so a call with any other client ID is refused with 403. Sign out at the top right when you are done. After 5 wrong passwords the login is locked for a short time. Use Forgot password? on the sign-in page to reset your password. For a new phone, or to remove someone who has left, email itedi@capacityllc.com.

Every current path starts with /api/v1/. Paths without /v1/ (for example /api/order/create) belong to the previous Capacity REST API and are kept only for integrations built against it. A new integration that calls one gets 410 Gone with the current path in the message. See the API reference, where those paths are marked deprecated.

Email itedi@capacityllc.com to request Partner API sandbox credentials. You receive: Item Example in these docs What it is Client ID YOUR_SANDBOX_CLIENT_ID Identifies your integration. Client secret YOUR_SANDBOX_CLIENT_SECRET A password for your integration. Case-sensitive. Owner code ZZ The 2-character code for your account. Reuse it until shortly before expires_in runs out; do not request a new token for every call. See Authentication for token caching. Check you are using sandbox credentials against the sandbox. 400 unsupported_grant_type grant_type is not client_credentials. Send grant_type=client_credentials. 503 temporarily_unavailable The token service is briefly unavailable. Wait a few seconds and retry.

Before you switch to production: Request production credentials. They are separate from your sandbox credentials. Change the base URL to the production URL. Keep it in configuration, not in code. Store the secret in a secrets manager, not in source control or logs. Reuse one token until shortly before it expires. Treat every date and time from the API as US Eastern time. See Dates and time zones. Retry 500, 503 and 504 with backoff, and send an X-Correlation-ID on every request so support can find it. See Errors.

Two calls report stock. Both take your 2-character owner code as client, matched exactly, including case. Call Use it for Get inventory Quantities per SKU: what you sell against. Get inventory by lot and LPN The same stock broken down by lot, expiry date and LPN (licence plate), with held quantity by reason code.

Nothing to report is null. In Get inventory, inventory is null rather than an empty list. Spelling and types. The field commited is spelled that way; price is a string. No expiry shows as 0001-01-01T00:00:00 in Get inventory by lot and LPN.
Stock changes as orders ship and receipts are put away. A few reads a day, and one an hour at most, keeps you in step; see Fair use.

This guide puts the outbound calls in the order an integration uses them. Each step links to its reference page for every field. Solid arrows are the order's progress in Capacity; dotted arrows are the calls you make to read it.

Submit orders (POST /api/v1/outbound/orders) takes one or more orders, each with its lines. You identify each order by your pick ticket (pickticketid); keep it unique per order. A 200 {"accepted": true} means the orders passed validation and are being created in the background, usually within seconds. Always send each order's lines: an order with an empty lines array is skipped without an error. The response carries no Capacity order IDs. Your pick ticket is how you refer to the order afterwards (cancel, ship confirmations). A requestedshipdate more than 3 days out normally holds the order as a future order until nearer the date. A 400 can mean some orders were accepted When individual orders fail validation, every valid order in the request is still accepted, and the 400 names one failed order and its reason, not every failure. Resend only the orders that failed: check each against the field rules to find them all. Nothing was accepted when the 400 is Invalid Input, Unable to validate client., or Please validate order data. with no detail. Do not resend orders automatically after a timeout If a Submit orders request times out with no response, the orders may have been accepted in full, and the API returns no order IDs you could check. Resending can create duplicate orders. Contact Capacity Support with the time of the request, the pick tickets and the X-Correlation-ID you sent. More on retries: Retrying order submissions.

Cancel an order (POST /api/v1/outbound/orders/cancel) cancels by pick ticket. Read order_cancelled in the 200 response: only open orders with no shipping or tracking information can be cancelled. If you cancel in the first seconds after submitting, the order may not exist yet; wait a few seconds and retry.

There are no callbacks: you poll. Capacity prepares ship confirmations in numbered batches per day. Ask your onboarding contact how many batches your account receives and when they are prepared. For each batch_date (US Eastern), request each batch_num after it has been prepared, with Get shipment confirmations (one item per order line) or Get shipment confirmations by carton (tracking number, SSCC and contents per carton). Match confirmations to your orders by pickticketid, and make processing idempotent: reading the same batch twice must not ship-confirm an order twice in your system. A batch with nothing in it is a 200 with {"message": "No records found. Please check input."}, not an empty list. A batch that has not been prepared yet looks the same, so do not treat an early empty answer as final. Batch 1 starts at 22:00 the evening before Ship-confirmation batches are keyed on when the confirmation was created (US Eastern), not the ship time. Batch 1 of a date covers confirmations created from 22:00 the previous evening; the other batches cover the calendar date. A confirmation created at 22:30 on 2 November is in batch 1 of 3 November. See the batch windows drawn out in Dates and time zones.
Get carrier tracking events returns carrier scans for one hour (hour_num 0-23, US Eastern) of a batch_date. Request an hour after it has ended. Events identify the order by capacityOrderNum.

Get order status returns the current status of the orders you send by Capacity order ID, with their lines, cartons and tracking. orderStatus is the order's latest status, so a shipped order shows as shipped. An order appears only once it has been picked: before that it comes back as "not found". Every order of yours that is currently picked is returned as well. To collect shipments in bulk, use step 3.

Submit receiving orders (POST /api/v1/inbound/orders) tells the fulfillment center what to expect. Send one element per PO line: clientcode, ponumber, deliverydate, sku and quantity are required on each. quantity is a whole number above 0. deliverydate is a US Eastern date. A 400 lists every problem found for a line, so you can fix them in one pass.

Get receipt confirmations works in batches, like ship confirmations: send batch_num (1 or more) and batch_date. receivedate is not the receipt time receivedate in the response is the time of your request, not the time the stock was received. Always send batch_date. A request without it is not rejected; it matches nothing. When there is nothing to report, the response is 200 with the plain string "Unable to find data for given request.".

What this means for you Ship-confirmation batches Formats Dates and times are US Eastern, with no offset Capacity operates on US Eastern time (America/New_York, EST/EDT). Every order, shipment, inventory and receiving date the Partner API accepts or returns is Eastern wall-clock time, and no time-zone offset is included. Convert explicitly; do not assume UTC. The one exception is the token's .issued and .expires, which are GMT.

Batch dates (batch_date) are Eastern calendar dates; see Ship-confirmation batches for the batch-1 window. Hours (hour_num on tracking events) are Eastern hours, 0–23. 0 is midnight to 00:59 Eastern. Dates you send on orders (orderdate, requestedshipdate, and so on) are read as Eastern dates. Daylight saving time applies. Eastern is UTC−5 in winter and UTC−4 in summer.

Batch 1 starts at 22:00 the evening before Ship-confirmation batches are keyed on when the confirmation was created (US Eastern), not the ship time. Batch 1 of a date covers confirmations created from 22:00 the previous evening; the other batches cover the calendar date. A confirmation created at 22:30 on 2 November is in batch 1 of 3 November. Error format Status codes No data is not an error Retrying order submissions Backoff Correlation IDs

Most errors from data endpoints are a JSON object with a message: { "message": "Please validate order data. Shipping Address 1 can not be empty for Pick Ticket Id PT-0001001" } Two exceptions: the token endpoint uses the OAuth error shape, and a failed order save on Submit orders returns {"accepted": false} (see Retrying order submissions). The token endpoint's error shape { "error": "invalid_credentials", "error_description": "A valid client_Id and client_Secret must be provided." } Match on the status code Read the HTTP status first, then the message. Messages are written for people; match on the status code in your code, not on message text.

Status Meaning Retry? What to do 200 Success. — Some read endpoints also return 200 when nothing matched; see No data is not an error. 400 The request is invalid: malformed JSON, a missing or invalid field, or your account could not be validated. No Fix the request. Validation messages name the field and the pick ticket. 401 Missing, malformed or expired token. Once, with a new token Get a new token and retry once. If it fails again, check your credentials. 404 None of the orders you asked for has been picked yet, and none is currently picked (Get order status). No Check the IDs; an order appears once it has been picked. 410 You called a path kept only for older integrations. No Use the current /api/v1/ path named in the message. 415 The Content-Type is not JSON. Returned only by Submit orders, Submit receiving orders, Get receipt confirmations, Get inventory and Get inventory by lot and LPN. No Send Content-Type: application/json (text/json is also accepted). 500 Something failed on our side. Yes, with backoff Retry. For order submission, see Retrying order submissions. 503 A service we depend on is briefly unavailable. Yes, with backoff Retry after a few seconds. 504 Returned instead of 500 for some accounts when orders could not be saved. Yes, with backoff Treat exactly like 500. The Partner API does not currently return 403, 409 or 429. Handle any other 4xx as "do not retry" and any other 5xx as "retry with backoff", so your integration keeps working if new codes are introduced.

When nothing matches, some read endpoints answer 200 with a message instead of an empty list: { "message": "No records found. Please check input." } Check the shape of a 200 body before you read it as data.

documents.t: Order submission is the one call where a retry could create duplicates, so it is handled specially. After a 400: A 400 can mean some orders were accepted When individual orders fail validation, every valid order in the request is still accepted, and the 400 names one failed order and its reason, not every failure. Resend only the orders that failed: check each against the field rules to find them all. Nothing was accepted when the 400 is Invalid Input, Unable to validate client., or Please validate order data. with no detail. After a 500 or 504 with {"accepted": false}: some orders may have been accepted. Resending the same request within 24 hours is generally safe: orders already accepted with identical content are recognised and skipped. After a timeout with no response at all: Do not resend orders automatically after a timeout If a Submit orders request times out with no response, the orders may have been accepted in full, and the API returns no order IDs you could check. Resending can create duplicate orders. Contact Capacity Support with the time of the request, the pick tickets and the X-Correlation-ID you sent.
Wait 2 seconds before the first retry, then double the wait each time (2, 4, 8, 16 seconds), adding up to a second of random jitter. Stop after five attempts and alert someone.

Send an X-Correlation-ID header with a unique value (a UUID) on every request. It is returned on the response. Log it with the request, and when you contact support quote it together with the time of the request and, for orders, the pick tickets.

The Partner API does not enforce request rate limits today. It serves every Capacity client from shared systems, so please follow these guidelines. If an integration's traffic affects other clients, Capacity may contact you. Call Recommended Get an access token Once per token lifetime (about 15 minutes). Cache the token; never request one per call. Submit orders As orders arrive, or grouped into one request every few minutes. Get shipment confirmations (both forms) Each batch after it has been prepared, not repeatedly through the day. Get carrier tracking events Each hour after it has ended, not repeatedly within the hour. Get inventory (both forms) A few times a day; once an hour at most. Get order status Once an hour at most. Test the connection For monitoring, once every 5 minutes at most.

Run scheduled jobs at a random minute, not exactly on the hour, so all integrations do not call at once. After an error, back off as described in Errors; never retry in a tight loop. Request the batches and hours you need, rather than re-reading a whole day.
If request limits are introduced, Capacity will announce them in the changelog. Handle any status code you do not recognise as described in Errors.

Change the base URL to https://api-partner.capacityllc.com and the token path to /api/v1/auth/token. Your credentials do not change. Change each path using the table above. Request and response bodies are the same, except for the two paths with no direct equivalent. Keep sending the key body field (and apiversion, if you send it today) until Capacity confirms your credentials are set up as a current integration; current integrations send neither. Test in the sandbox before switching production.

partner-api.v1.json is the complete v1 contract (OpenAPI 3). It is generated from the API itself, so it always matches the API reference. Use it to generate a client, to import into an API tool such as Postman, Insomnia or Bruno, or to see what changed between versions.

The collection holds the requests used throughout these docs, with a script that gets and reuses an access token for you. Download the collection and the Sandbox environment (Production environment). In Postman, choose Import and select both files. Select the Sandbox environment. Fill in clientId and clientSecret with your sandbox credentials. Keep the secret in the current value only, so it is never synced or shared. Send Test the connection. The token is fetched automatically. The example values (owner code ZZ, SKU-EXAMPLE-1, the pick ticket) are placeholders: replace them with your account's values before sending orders. Dates are filled in when you send a request, on the US Eastern calendar: the ship date a week out and the batch date today.
The version is in the path: every current operation is under /api/v1/.

These changes are not breaking. They can be made to v1 at any time and are listed in the changelog. Build your integration so that they do not break it: New operations. New optional request fields. New response fields. Ignore fields you do not recognise. New status codes. Handle an unknown 4xx as "do not retry" and an unknown 5xx as "retry with backoff". Changed message text. Match on the status code, never on the message.
documents.s: Changes that can happen within v1

documents.t: These are breaking: removing or renaming a field or operation, making an optional field required, changing a field's type or format, or tightening a limit such as a maximum length. Capacity checks every change to the API's contract for breaking changes before it is released. A breaking change to v1 is listed in the changelog.

The paths of the previous Capacity REST API are kept for existing integrations and marked deprecated in the OpenAPI document. New integrations must use the /api/v1/ paths; see Previous REST API paths.
The complete v1 contract is published at /openapi/partner-api.v1.json. It changes whenever the API reference on this site changes, so you can generate a client from it or compare versions.

Email the Capacity integrations team at itedi@capacityllc.com for: sandbox or production credentials replacing a credential that may have been exposed help with a failing request questions about the API if you are evaluating Capacity Existing clients with a production problem: email itsupport@capacityllc.com to open a support ticket, or contact your Capacity account manager.

Help us find your request quickly: The environment (sandbox or production) The method and path, for example POST /api/v1/outbound/orders The X-Correlation-ID you sent, and the time of the request (with time zone) The HTTP status and the response body Never include your client secret or an access token in a ticket or email.
